palette.notes: Clip: indexed palette grid with ranges reserved for water (blue-white steps), foliage greens and warm stone; a night version shifts the whole grid to dark blues with a few warm lights.

lighting: Lighting is the palette: swapping the whole palette turns the same day waterfall into a dark night scene with only warm lantern pixels left lit.
silhouette: Detailed painterly scene (cliffs, pagodas, waterfall, trees); the pixels never move, so silhouettes are fixed and the motion lives inside them.

motion.timing: Pixels stay still while palette entries rotate in order; the demo runs at 60 fps with a speed control. Blend mode fades between steps for smoother flow.

texture: Dense dithered painting; water and falls are bands of 4-8 related colours laid in streaks so rotating them reads as flowing water.
camera: Locked full-scene view; the clip only zooms to show the palette grid next to the image.

acting.enters: No characters; the scene itself changes from day to night.
acting.acts: Water falls and shimmers forever by cycling colours, and the whole scene relights when the palette changes.
acting.depth: Depth comes from painting (misty, lighter far cliffs, dark close foliage), not from movement.

techniques: rotate a reserved palette range to make water, lava or lights move
lay the cycling colours in streaks along the flow direction
swap the whole palette for time of day: same pixels, new mood
blend mode: fade between steps for smooth flow
marquee-bulb chase for blinking lights and signs
feel: still painted scene + rotating water colours + whole-palette night swap = alive without moving a pixel
for_fred: Make Fred's pond water flow by cycling 4-6 blue steps instead of animating frames, and use a palette swap for a 'later that night' beat (same scene, dark blues, one warm lamp) so Fred's comeback reads as time passing.
